content.text:
The drawing shows a quinazoline core with three substituents.

- **Core:** a quinazoline with N1 and N3 in the pyrimidine ring. C2 sits between the two nitrogens and carries the NH-aryl group. C4 carries a phenyl. The fused benzene ring carries a furan-2-yl group at C6.
- **C2 substituent:** an NH linked to a para-substituted benzene ring bearing SO2NH2, i.e. a 4-sulfamoylphenylamino group.
- **C6 position:** C4a is attached to C4. Going around the benzo ring from C4a, the next carbon is C5 (the CH at the lower left of the ring), and C6 is the carbon carrying the furan. In the drawing, the furan-bearing carbon is the left-lower carbon, adjacent to the C5 CH, which is adjacent to C4a. This matches C6.

SMILES, written from C2 outward:
- C2: `c1(Nc2ccc(cc2)S(N)(=O)=O)nc(-c2ccccc2)c2cc(-c3ccco3)ccc2n1`
- Ring closure: N3 connects to C4, C4 to C4a, C4a to C5, C5 to C6 (furan), then C7, C8, C8a, and N1 back to C2.

SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(Nc2nc(-c3ccccc3)c3cc(-c4ccco4)ccc3n2)cc1
